name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify a Domainry backend from accepted requirements or delivered frontend evidence. Use for metadata-first Domainry projects, frontend-to-Runtime replacement, Runtime integration, and full-stack defect routing. Keeps frontend evidence read-only except an explicitly authorized Data Exchange offline-export center.
---

# Domainry Builder V1

Each run owns one explicit Delivery Batch and follows exactly `requirements → model → apply → verify → done`. A batch is an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Keep one project-visible TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md`; copy [the template](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md) only when it is absent, then resume its `Current stage`. Do not invent stages, state files, or continuation workflows.

The accepted product scope remains the baseline: never silently reduce it to an MVP. Put stable Requirement IDs and Feature keys in the current batch, record deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership, and include every shared resource or regression boundary affected by the batch. `done` means this batch is complete, not that deferred product scope was delivered.

Resolve this file's directory as `SKILL_ROOT` and set `DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"`. Use only that packaged CLI. The workflow has exactly five commands: `model capability`, `model plan`, `apply model`, `apply finalize`, and `verify`.

## requirements

Read [requirements and domain truth](references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md) and the [PRD template](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). Settle domain truth inside this stage for the current batch and its dependency closure: actors and scope; objects, relations, states, defaults, and retention; commands, transactions, idempotency, calculations, and external effects; Reports and offline export intent; schedules, notifications, files, and integrations. `workspace` is Domainry's tenant boundary, not a peer of a separate tenant concept: translate tenant wording in requirements to workspace context, and never author a `tenant` or `workspace` Object/table, project-owned `tenant_id`/`workspace_id`, or duplicate workspace identity/projection. A company, customer, merchant, store, or other independently required business aggregate must use its actual domain name and lifecycle, never `tenant` as an infrastructure surrogate. Any required human approve/reject wait is a Runtime Workflow requirement, not two synchronous Handler branches. Any required downloadable Report export is a governed `report_export_controls` plus offline Data Exchange requirement, not a Report permission alone.

When frontend source exists, inspect it as evidence, including API Mock adapters, handlers, fixtures, seeds, and mutation side effects. `frontend/**` is read-only except for the authorized export-center slice described below. Treat it as evidence, not authority for missing policy. Record frontend defects for owner `frontend`; do not hide them with backend workarounds. Preserve the accepted product baseline in `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` and record a traceable current-batch delta with stable Requirement IDs, sources, owners, acceptance results, Feature ownership and deferred scope. Do not advance while an unresolved choice changes current-batch observable behavior, authorization, money/units, an irreversible effect, or state flow.

## model

Select the one task profile and comma-separated requirement topics from the accepted current-batch dependency closure, then request one exact minimum reading plan. Its `capability_contracts` is the complete inlined machine-contract closure for that scope; do not scan the [capability index](references/capabilities/README.md) or issue one `model capability --key` call per category. Read every returned `read_order` path once, in order, relative to `SKILL_ROOT`. The returned documents, including [backend model](references/backend-model.md) when selected, remain authoritative—the plan removes discovery calls, not semantics. Preserve the complete current desired state in `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`; prefer one Feature per model file, and change only current-batch Features plus the declared shared-resource closure. Never edit `domain/**` or `.domainry/**`, and never emit compiler-owned `capability_assembly`, standalone Permission definitions, versions, ownership, or seed metadata. Author each ordinary human Role directly as an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` grants; that shorthand expands to the published `any`/`manual`/workspace-provisioned defaults. In `project.initial_workspace_administrator_role`, explicitly select the one Role assigned to the first Workspace administrator; it must be workspace-provisioned, use `audience:any|user`, use `assignment_mode:manual`, and have no `required_binding_key`. Never infer this selection from a Role suffix, risk level, permissions, ordering, or the first Role. Use an extended Role with `audience: "service"` and `assignment_mode: "system_managed"` for an internal Workflow/Scheduler execution identity, and omit `provision_to_workspaces` (preferred) or set it to false; bind that Role by key through Workflow `run_as`, including a Workflow targeted by Scheduler. Never convert an internal role into a human tenant-login actor to satisfy validation.

Classify every writable Object as either plain `direct_crud`, or `action_only` plus a source-owned Handler for any named, conditional, derived, state-changing, side-effecting, or cross-record command. Do not author new Automation. A human approval must be an enabled Workflow graph with an approval task, authorized assignee resolver, explicit approved and rejected branches, and terminal Action effects; standalone approve/reject Handlers are not the waiting process. Reports use `object_sql_v1`; inside its SQL, wrap every model-derived Object and field identifier in MySQL backticks even when the key is not a SQL keyword, while keeping aliases, parameter names, and result aliases unquoted. A bounded same-Object aggregate across Runtime-installed Workspaces uses the separate `cross-workspace-aggregate` topic and never caller SQL or Workspace IDs. Use `organization-delivery` for Runtime-selected ownership targets and store provisioning, `identity-handler-delivery` for atomic Identity/Profile delivery, and `workspace-identity-usage` for installation-authorized account counts. Every required export also authors the Blueprint `report_export_controls` closure (bounded rows, audit/download Objects and mappings, requester-owned grants, assurance/masking when required) while Runtime Report and Data Exchange own execution.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --reading-profile <initial-delivery|feature-increment|handler-repair> \
  --topics <records,permissions,identity-profile,identity-handler-delivery,organization,organization-delivery,reporting-line,workflow,scheduler,reports,report-export,cross-workspace-aggregate,workspace-identity-usage,notifications,connectors,agents,entrypoints,workspace-provisioning,files,domain-truth>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`model plan` performs one immutable load of the complete current model, validates the whole cross-resource draft, derives capability and authorization closure, persists deterministic diagnostics/provenance, and reports the Ledger change set. On failure, repair the complete stdout `diagnostics` batch using each file/JSON Pointer, constraint, actual/allowed value and hint before rerunning; its `artifact` path, relative to `--project`, retains the full provenance. Use only the exact contract keys returned in `capability_contracts`; Runtime execution-only modules have none. A Delivery Batch is not a loader or apply filter. Confirm that every create, update and delete belongs to the batch or its declared impact closure; repair the named owner and rerun. Once valid, keep the model unchanged while reviewing removals and evolution-sensitive changes.

## apply

Read [project mutation](references/project-mutation.md), then apply the reviewed model:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module>
```

Gate on the returned state before reading or writing implementation source. `implementation_ready` or `applied` is materialized success. `evolution_review_required` is an exit-0, non-terminal control state with `materialization_state:not_materialized`: inspect the exact immutable `evolution_audit_path` and `evolution_audit_sha256`, then rerun the returned `next_command` after replacing its reason placeholder with a non-empty explanation of the reviewed diff. Do not continue to source implementation or finalization until that reapply returns `implementation_ready` or `applied`; a stale SHA, omitted SHA/reason, or failed repair remains a non-zero failure. On successful reapply, `evolution_source_finalization.state:deferred_unfinalized_source` means the audit proved the previous delivery had never been finalized: the reviewed in-progress source was preserved, not trusted or finalized, and the ordinary focused-test/`apply finalize` gate remains mandatory. Never delete an existing finalization receipt to force this state; its file SHA is bound into the audit.

Retain the immutable implementation packet only from a materialized-success response. Read the compact packet index once: its `actions` array is the complete exact Action-context path list, `summary.shared_constraints` applies to every Action, and `summary.test_commands` is the copyable command contract for this delivery. Read its exact `verification.path` core during apply—not after finalization—then read each shard in `verification.minimum_read_plan` exactly once after checking its published byte count and SHA-256; those shards contain only the listed `route_keys` reachable from this project's compiled manifest. Never enumerate or read unlisted route artifacts, and never read the full source route catalog—the core's `route_catalog` identity preserves its completeness. Before authoring any business-flow source, consume `evidence_contract` as the complete marker grammar: use its allowed `source` values and numeric `requirement_id_pattern`, and implement every flow-specific `required_operations` entry with its exact source and `required_observations` (BF08 publishes all seven governed-export steps). Copy `verification.harness_template.path` verbatim to `backend/tests/businessflow/harness_test.go` and author scenarios rather than regenerating transport, authentication, response-decoding, and evidence infrastructure. Consume `setup_contract`, compact `routes`, and the focused shards directly. Build every business-flow precondition for an `action_only` Object through a published authored Action; when a flow needs business actors or organizations, use an authored Identity HandlerDelivery or OrganizationDelivery Action. Bootstrap materializes the Blueprint's eligible human Workspace Roles, assigns only the explicitly selected `initial_workspace_administrator_role` to the first administrator, and keeps service/system-managed Roles out of tenant login provisioning. If the authored Action surface cannot establish an exact required state, repair the Blueprint and Handler contract before finalization, rerun `model plan`, then follow `setup_contract.post_apply_repair`; never inject records, roles, users, organizations, or historical timestamps through a startup fixture. Then read each compact Action context by exact path and follow that context's `read_order` once, in order, relative to `PROJECT_ROOT/backend`; those exact generated contracts and project-owned source/test files replace embedded source dumps and broad generated-tree scans. For this packet, implement only the project-owned backend source and paired tests, and create every required `backend/tests/businessflow` case for this batch. Every multi-item command or query uses one generated batch/bulk capability call; never loop over a single-item capability or Runtime API to simulate batch behavior, including through helper indirection. Pure in-memory loops are allowed only when needed to build bounded batch inputs or correlate results and must contain no capability I/O. If the required true-batch primitive is absent, repair the owning contract instead of hiding the gap with pseudo-batch code; use a bounded sequential fallback only when true batch cannot be implemented and the accepted requirement explicitly defines its non-atomic, partial-failure semantics. For a selected custom Connector, request its focused context with `model capability --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementation. Never edit generated source, manifests, receipts, caches, journals, or managed Runtime state.

The only frontend mutation exception is a Data Exchange offline-export center for an exportable Object SQL Report when `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; follow [its contract](references/frontend-offline-report-export.md). Otherwise report the owner gap.

Follow `summary.stage_boundary` literally: finish all project-owned source, then run `summary.test_commands.focused` and `summary.test_commands.business_flow_compile` before finalization; a full-tree failure caused by not-yet-generated composition is not an implementation failure. The shared harness is a template copied into project-owned tests, never imported from `.domainry`. After both pre-finalize commands pass run `summary.test_commands.finalize`, then and only then run `summary.test_commands.full_tree`. These commands already contain the backend working directory, delivery build constraint, and project-local-plus-public hybrid `GOPROXY`; do not replace them with a default or local-only proxy. Once finalization succeeds, project-owned source is frozen for this verification attempt. Any later source change starts a new repair iteration and requires the focused/compile/finalize sequence again; do not continue the stale attempt into `verify`.

Finalize every delivered Handler and Connector:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`apply finalize` enforces source call-site contracts, including guarded `ConditionalUpdate` and the no-pseudo-batch invariant across capability aliases, callbacks, and named local helper call chains; do not add manual grep gates. Run the affected backend test set before advancing.

## verify

Read [evidence levels](references/evidence-levels.md), [verification](references/verification.md), and [Runtime integration](references/backend-runtime.md). The implementation packet's verification guide and every required business-flow test must already have been consumed/completed during apply. Verify is read-and-run only: do not create, edit, rename, or delete project-owned source after finalization. Every current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary needs a complete project-owned case with explicit preconditions, ordered actions, and a terminal durable result; denial cases also prove unchanged state. For every module HTTP step, resolve the exact route in the implementation packet and grant that route's `authorization.permission` with its `required_role_grant.data_scope` to the selected actor Role before finalization; Report audience/source data access never substitutes for the executable route Permission. Decode Runtime record pages only as top-level `items`, with business fields in each `items[].data` and record metadata such as `id`/`updated_at` on the item envelope. Unchanged flows may reuse only current baseline evidence. Run the highest-risk changed case against the managed Runtime before broader flow verification.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

`verify` reuses structural/package receipts only after their complete source, model, Runtime and dependency identities validate; otherwise it runs the complete backend tree and rebuilds. It always proves healthy start and same-cohort restart, then leaves Runtime stopped and emits stage/cache telemetry. `backend/tests/businessflow` is a black-box Runtime package: it may use published Runtime HTTP/client operations but never import project Handlers, generated capability/data fakes, or database drivers. For both phases every BF01-BF08 test emits its structured evidence marker exactly as verification documents. Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque. A shared login, health, read, or Action-catalog probe does not prove another named flow; each claimed Runtime case must execute its own ordered Runtime journey and read back its terminal durable result. Approval cases start the Workflow, observe the task, prove unauthorized denial, decide both branches, and read back process/task/business state. Export cases query and prepare the governed Report export, follow the requester-owned Data Exchange job to completion/download, and prove another actor is denied. Verify only requirement-observable denial, scope, conflict, rollback, replay, restart, worker, Report, export, file, notification, and provider behavior. Do not create a project evidence ledger or generic acceptance runner.

## done

Set `Current stage: done` only when every current-batch finding is resolved and current receipts, tests, durable observations, and Runtime identity support the claim. Report batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, tests, Runtime result, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations without claiming deferred product work is complete.

Project-owned edits are limited to requirements/TODO evidence, declarative model/SQL, backend source/tests, and the authorized export-center exception. Recoverable failures stay in the current stage: repair the responsible owner and rerun the same direct command.
# Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

Preserve the full accepted product demand as the requirements baseline. For a new project, complete replacement, or existing project increment, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`, or record an equivalent traceable current-batch delta that references the unchanged accepted baseline. Never silently reduce product demand to an MVP.

One Delivery Batch may implement an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Record its stable Requirement IDs, planned Feature keys, baseline delivery/model identity, allowed shared-resource changes and affected regression boundary. Requirements outside the batch remain explicit deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership; `done` closes only the batch. A Feature slice must be dependency-closed: include any shared Role, entrypoint, Object, Action, Report, lifecycle or authorization change required for its behavior to be valid and verifiable.

Settle domain truth completely for the current batch and dependency closure before capability discovery. Deferred slices need enough stable identity and ownership to remain visible, but their unresolved details do not block this batch unless they change its observable result, authorization, amount/unit semantics, irreversible effect, or state flow. A later batch reuses the accepted baseline and resolves its own delta instead of rewriting unrelated requirements.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/handlers and fixtures/seeds; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Requirements inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

When the frontend is already implemented, do not stop at API method names or TypeScript types. Search for every API dependency's Mock implementation, including request handlers, success/error responses, fixture collections, seeded identities, mutation side effects, generated identifiers, relation keys, enum/status values, timestamps, totals, and nested objects. Reconcile those concrete values with component reads and writes. Add any evidenced missing object, field, relation, lifecycle state, query shape, or representative worked example to the PRD, with its exact source path and an appropriate classification. Preserve conflicts and optionality: Mock-only fields remain `recommended` or `open` unless higher-precedence evidence confirms them, and decorative/test-only values do not become domain facts.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per in-scope requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Feature key → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and route touched by the batch; reference the accepted baseline for unchanged rows and preserve explicit dispositions for deferred rows. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle only the model-visible Report facts: the business question, Object SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Report query transport and export execution are Runtime-owned and stay out of the project model and PRD.

Every required Report export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job. When the project owns a frontend, the PRD also records the export-center route/audience and the actor-visible job-list/download outcome. If the active typed Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned Data Exchange export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap instead of inventing a route or browser-local list.

Verify the authorized Object SQL result, out-of-scope denial, offline job submission, actor-owned job-list visibility, and completed-file download when export is required. Do not turn Runtime execution internals into project acceptance cases.

Record any explicitly required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as a business-flow verification obligation. Capability schemas are resolved during model routing; do not manufacture a separate platform gate catalog or case inventory.

Every write row must define authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry, and durable outcome. Runtime-owned codes and reversible mechanism choices may cite their decision row rather than becoming product blockers.

## 6. Calculations and policy versions

Distinguish occurred facts, summaries, and simulations before selecting any Runtime capability. Every material calculation row must close all business ownership and reproducibility columns. Exact decimal representation, an explicit comparison threshold, or summation remains modelable when currency, unit, or range metadata is absent: keep optional metadata nullable and enforce stated command preconditions. Only two or more incompatible unit/formula interpretations that change the explicitly required result block the smallest affected comparison/conversion or calculation slice. Runtime representations and reversible mechanics follow their nonblocking decision classes.

| Requirement ID | Fact type (`occurred` / `summary` / `simulation`) | Result | Inputs and units | Formula | Calculation Owner | Evaluation Time | Persisted Result | Policy/Rule Snapshot | Input Snapshot | Calculation Trace | Rounding point and mode | Correction/Reversal Strategy | Downstream Consumers | Report Source of Truth | Worked examples | Classification | Confirmation evidence |

## 7. Authorization, data scope, and navigation

An explicit update/delete denial can be modeled without a business read actor. When business-role read is not required, use formal admin/seed or persistence evidence for creation proof and do not invent business read permission merely to make acceptance convenient.

## 8. Reports, Agent tasks, schedules, notifications, files, and integrations

An asynchronous approval with explicit approved/rejected outcomes may keep pending on an independent approval Object when the host lifecycle defines no pending state; the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect. Unspecified edit/cancel/resubmit behavior is nonblocking, with conservative no-expansion concurrency/idempotency that prevents duplicate effects. For an explicit weekday/morning schedule without timezone or holiday-calendar preference, use the platform/deployment-configured deterministic timezone and standard weekday cron and record the preference as a follow-up. Do not block unless an explicitly required multi-timezone or statutory-holiday distinction changes the demanded outcome.

### Object SQL Report and offline export contract

The project model exposes only Object SQL Reports. Record each Report's business purpose, SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Runtime owns Report query transport and export execution. Every required export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job; the owned frontend must provide one export-center list/download experience when frontend integration is authorized.

| Requirement ID | Capability | Owner / trigger / schedule | Inputs | Durable output / audit | Agent side-effect mode or Connector/external effect | Identity / allowlist / retry / reconciliation | Permission / scope | Classification | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Requirement ID / Report key | Business question / result meaning | SQL source of truth | Parameters / defaults | Result columns / types | Required permission / audience / data scope | Export required | Expected query result | Expected offline export result | Export-center route / audience | Data Exchange list/download support or owner gap | Evidence |

## Backend dependency PRD

Preserve the full accepted product demand as the requirements baseline. For a new project, complete replacement, or existing project increment, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`, or record an equivalent traceable current-batch delta that references the unchanged accepted baseline. Never silently reduce product demand to an MVP.

One Delivery Batch may implement an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Record its stable Requirement IDs, planned Feature keys, baseline delivery/model identity, allowed shared-resource changes and affected regression boundary. Requirements outside the batch remain explicit deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership; `done` closes only the batch. A Feature slice must be dependency-closed: include any shared Role, entrypoint, Object, Action, Report, lifecycle or authorization change required for its behavior to be valid and verifiable.

Settle domain truth completely for the current batch and dependency closure before capability discovery. Deferred slices need enough stable identity and ownership to remain visible, but their unresolved details do not block this batch unless they change its observable result, authorization, amount/unit semantics, irreversible effect, or state flow. A later batch reuses the accepted baseline and resolves its own delta instead of rewriting unrelated requirements.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Requirements inspection is read-only. Preserve conflicts and optionality: Mock-only fields remain `recommended` or `open` unless higher-precedence evidence confirms them, and decorative/test-only values do not become domain facts.

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;

4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle only the model-visible Report facts: the business question, Object SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Report query transport and export execution are Runtime-owned and stay out of the project model and PRD.

Every required Report export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job. If the active typed Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned Data Exchange export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap instead of inventing a route or browser-local list.

Verify the authorized Object SQL result, out-of-scope denial, offline job submission, actor-owned job-list visibility, and completed-file download when export is required. Do not turn Runtime execution internals into project acceptance cases.

The fragment assumes the referenced Object and Action exist in the complete
Feature closure. `provision_to_workspaces: true` means tenant login
materialization and is invalid on this internal role.

If this scheduled business flow evaluates an elapsed-time cutoff that must be
proved in a short-lived isolated Runtime, author the specific evaluation Action
with an optional standalone `evaluation_time: "datetime"` input from the first
Blueprint. The service-only Workflow Action may receive it in black-box
verification; the ordinary Scheduler path omits it, and the Handler uses real
current time when it is absent. Never turn this into a global clock override,
a human grant, or a startup historical fixture. The `scheduler.authoring`
`elapsed_time_verification` machine contract is authoritative for this seam.

## Delivery batches and file ownership

Whole-model validation does not require whole-product implementation. The files
currently present under `backend/model/*.json` are the complete desired-state
baseline for this delivery. A Delivery Batch is an authoring and verification
scope, not a loader or apply filter: preserve every previously applied model
file, then add or update only the batch's Feature files and declared
shared-resource closure. `model plan` and `apply model` continue to load and
validate the complete current model atomically.

Prefer `00-project.json` plus one Feature per descriptively named model file.
Several files may declare different Features under the same module. A Role,
entrypoint or other cross-cutting resource still has one owning Feature/file;
when it supports multiple Features, declare those stable keys through the
resource `requirements` override instead of repeating the resource.

The Feature key is also its Requirement identity. Moving one intact Feature to
another file does not change Ledger identity, but splitting or renaming a
Feature creates new Requirement identities, relinks affected resources and may
delete the old Requirement. Review that change with `model plan`; never treat it
as a mechanical file edit. For an already-applied oversized Feature, a valid
staged migration may retain the old Feature as a requirement-only umbrella,
move one resource group per batch to a new Feature, and temporarily link those
resources to both Requirement keys. Retire the umbrella only in a later,
explicitly reviewed destructive batch when it no longer represents accepted
product demand.

The V2 `items -> module -> kind -> item -> payload -> emits` envelope is not
accepted. Do not author `kind`, `status`, `depends_on`, `decisions`,
`requirement_keys`, `contract_version`, `capability_assembly`, or internal
Ledger item names. This project is not released yet, so there is no legacy
format fallback.

## Feature ownership and traceability

Every resource inside a Feature inherits that Feature's requirement. Plane
creates the requirement Ledger item, resource dependencies and behavior links.
Only a resource shared by multiple Features declares an override:

```json
{
  "objects": {
    "item": {
      "requirements": ["item_lifecycle", "audit_requirement"],
      "fields": {"name": "text!"}
    }
  }
}
```

`requirement` contains only `statement` and optional non-empty `acceptance`.
Behavior owner tuples and the no-executable reason are compiler output.

## Keyed identities everywhere

Every schema array whose item has a stable identity is authored as a keyed
object. The compiler sorts it, injects `key`, `id`, `object_key`, `path`, or
`connection_key` as required, and emits the strongly typed array. This includes
Objects, Fields, Roles, Actions, dictionary items, report parameters/result
columns, notification variables, Workflow inputs/nodes/edges and Agent
resources. An unchanged baseline Automation follows the same keyed-instruction
shape when it is loaded, but this Skill does not author a new Automation.
Repeating the identity inside a value or using an identity-bearing array fails
model loading.

Within a Workflow resource, `input_fields` and graph children remain keyed
maps (Actions use `input`, not `input_fields`):

```json
{"input_fields": {"comment": "long_text!"}}
```

```json
{
  "graph": {
    "nodes": {
      "start": {"type": "trigger"},
      "finish": {
        "type": "action",
        "contract": {
          "action": {"action_key": "item.finish", "on_error": "fail"}
        }
      }
    },
    "edges": {
      "start_finish": {"source": "start", "target": "finish"}
    }
  }
}
```

State transitions use their directed edge as identity, so duplicate edges are
structurally impossible:

```json
{"transitions": {"draft->submitted": "item.submit", "submitted->archived": {"workflow": "item.archive"}}}
```

Open maps remain maps. In particular Agent `input_schema`/`output_schema`
properties, Action/Workflow bindings, connector configuration and other
business dictionaries are not mistaken for resource arrays.

Author every platform-defined closed enum with its documented canonical
spelling (normally lower_snake_case; Report `currency` is lowercase). Plane
accepts mixed-case spellings for compatibility and canonicalizes them before
validation, including nested schema enums, Role scopes, Handler access
operations and field DSL vocabulary. This compatibility never applies to
identity-bearing keys or open business values; those retain their declared
case and stable identifiers remain strict lowercase.

## Field string DSL

Object Fields, Action `input`/`output`, Workflow inputs and Report SQL
parameters use the complete compact base grammar:

```text
<type>[!][->target][value[:label]|...][=default][;modifier[=value]]...
```

### Complete type and modifier quick reference

This is the single copyable reference for the field DSL. It contains every
supported field type and every Object-field modifier; capability references
should link here instead of repeating the table.

```json
{
  "active": "boolean=true",
  "amount": "currency!=0;precision=19;scale=2;currency=CNY;rounding=half_even",
  "effective_date": "date!",
  "starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00",
  "contact_email": "email!;max_length=254",
  "quantity": "integer!;min=1;max=999",
  "remark": "long_text;min_length=1;max_length=500;localized",
  "score": "number;min=0;max=100",
  "discount_rate": "percent;precision=5;scale=2;rounding=half_even",
  "contact_phone": "phone;pattern=^\\+[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$",
  "customer_id": "relation!->customer;cardinality=many_to_one;on_delete=restrict;inverse=invoices",
  "status": "select![draft:草稿|done:完成]=draft",
  "business_no": "text!;unique;indexed",
  "website": "url",
  "assignee": "user",
  "category": "select!;dictionary=case_category",
  "risk_level": "select!;value_domain=risk_level"
}
```

- `!` means required.
- A default belongs in the base specification before the first modifier:
  `currency!=0;precision=19`, never `currency!;precision=19;=0`.
- `relation` requires `->target` and never accepts a default.
- `select` requires a non-empty, unique stable vocabulary. Labels default from
  the stable value when omitted.
- Supported non-relation Object modifiers are `unique`, `indexed`, `localized`,
  `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `precision`, `scale`,
  `currency`, `rounding`, `cardinality`, `on_delete`, `inverse`, `dictionary`,
  and `value_domain`.
- A relation never accepts `unique`; use `cardinality=one_to_one`, which makes
  the compiler derive uniqueness.
- Unknown types/modifiers, duplicates, invalid values, out-of-vocabulary
  defaults and context-inapplicable modifiers fail closed.
- Field types, modifier names and closed platform enum values are
  case-insensitive on input and compile to their documented lowercase values.
  ISO currency codes compile to uppercase. Stable business identities such as
  field keys, relation targets, option values, dictionaries and value domains
  remain strict lowercase identifiers.

Common repairs are local to the rejected field string:

| Rejected | Use | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"customer_id": "relation!"` | `"customer_id": "relation!->customer"` | A relation requires its target. |
| `"status": "select!"` | `"status": "select![draft\|done]"` | Select needs exactly one vocabulary source. |
| `"status": "select![draft];dictionary=status"` | Choose inline options or `dictionary`, not both. | Vocabulary sources are exclusive. |
| `"amount": "currency;precision=2;scale=3"` | `"amount": "currency;precision=19;scale=2"` | Scale cannot exceed precision. |
| `"amount": "currency!;precision=19;=0"` | `"amount": "currency!=0;precision=19"` | A default must precede every modifier. |
| `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03 09:00"` | `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00"` | Datetime defaults use RFC3339. |

The CLI rejects an invalid string during model loading and reports the stable
diagnostic code, exact JSON path, field key and repair facts. Fix that string;
do not replace the compact field map with generated full field arrays.

Notification variables use only the restricted `<type>[!]` subset. Their types
are `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `email`, `number`, `text`, and `url`; they do
not accept select options, relation targets, defaults, or modifiers. A business
enum such as `select![approved|rejected]` is rendered text in a notification, so
author it as `text!` and retain the enum on its owning Object or Action field.

Plane expands Object fields to `key`, `name`, `type`, `required`, `config`,
`validation`, labeled `options`, `unique` and `default_value`. Human-readable
names default from stable keys (`item_submission` -> `Item Submission`). Object
descriptions also receive a deterministic non-empty default; provide explicit
text only when it carries real domain meaning.

Action fields use the same strings. Object-only modifiers are consistency
assertions whose source Plane uniquely infers from the owning Object and the
Handler access closure, as detailed below. This preserves the named
type/precision contract without exposing source pointers to the model.

## Actions and source-owned Handlers

An Action key is exactly `<object_key>.<action_key>`; Plane derives
`object_key`, the default name, audit metadata, same-key Permission and empty
contracts. The model decides `kind`, allowed business roles, business fields,
preconditions and whether a source-owned Handler is needed.

`object_create` is the Runtime-owned generic single-Object create and must not
carry a project Handler. Use `object_operation` plus Handler/access when an
object-scoped create must derive trusted owner/org values, coordinate multiple
Objects, or execute other project logic. All other supported Handler kinds and
their object/record invocation scope are listed in the Actions capability
reference. A Handler Action must not use the bare suffix `create`, `read`,
`update`, `delete`, `restore`, `import`, or `export`, because those exact
`<object>.<operation>` keys belong to Runtime Object Permissions. Use a business
verb such as `lead.register` or a qualified key such as `lead.create_owned`;
grant that exact Action key to the Role.

```json
{
  "actions": {
    "invoice.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "input": {"comment": "long_text!", "effective_date": "date!"},
      "output": {"status": "select![approved|rejected]"},
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval updates the invoice and durable decision atomically",
        "access": {
          "invoice": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "approval_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`handler.reason` is the only authored capability-gap/rationale statement.
Plane derives owner, trigger, scope, atomicity, rollback semantics, involved
Objects, read/write sets and transaction requirement. Do not author
`authorization`, `payload_fields`, `handler.data_access`, `handler.output`,
`audit_event`, empty defaults, or behavior tuples.

An aggregate-only Handler may omit `access` when it declares
`cross_workspace_aggregates`; Plane emits empty raw `data_access` and derives
the fixed source Object into the read-effect closure. Use the
`cross-workspace-aggregate` reading topic for the closed dimensions, optional
source-owned date bucket, measures, filters, authorization, result schema, and
Runtime limit contract. Grain, IANA time zone, and Workspace selection are not
caller input.

A Handler may likewise omit `access` when its complete effect is expressed by
the narrow Foundation capabilities `target_organization`,
`store_organization_catalog`, `store_organization_mutations`,
`workspace_identity_usage`, or
`identity_handler_delivery`. These declarations compile into fixed generated
methods and descriptor grants; they do not authorize raw Object reads/writes or
generic Identity/Organization APIs. Load the `organization-delivery`,
`identity-handler-delivery`, or `workspace-identity-usage` reading topic before
authoring one of them. Identity/Profile mutation effects needed by a declared
profile binding are compiler-owned closure and must not be repeated as
`handler.access`.

Keep a plain Action-only value as a plain field DSL such as `"reason": "long_text"`;
it does not need a backing Object field. When an Action field
uses Object-only modifiers (for example `max_length`) or Object-backed numeric
semantics, Plane infers its source from the owning Object plus the Objects in
`handler.access`, using the Action field's exact key only. The owning Object wins
over an equally named field elsewhere in the access closure; equally ranked
same-key fields fail as ambiguous. Plane never binds differently named fields
through Action verbs, prefixes, suffixes, stemming, edit distance, grammar, or
synonyms. When an Action input and persisted Object field represent the same
business datum, give them the same stable key, for example
`rejection_reason` end to end. Otherwise remove Object-only modifiers to keep
the Action value standalone. The diagnostic lists compatible rename candidates
without choosing one. Never author a source pointer or add a fake Object field.
This source is generated type/lineage reuse only; it does not copy an Object
field's runtime value into the Action payload.

For `identity_handler_delivery`, keep Identity-owned, non-Profile inputs such
as `login_id`, `display_name`, `role_key`, and `manager` standalone: use plain
DSL such as `email!`, `text!`, `select![employee|manager]`, or `user`, without
Object-only modifiers. A Profile-bound value may reuse Object-only modifiers
only when the owning Object or an Object in `handler.access` has an exact
same-key compatible field. Read the `identity-handler-delivery` topic for a
complete Action input and Profile example; never add a fake Object field.

Two fixed Store Organization mutation inputs are the deliberate exception to
same-key Object source inference. For an exact `rename` grant,
`store_name: text!;max_length=200` and
`expected_store_version: integer!;min=1` belong to the Identity capability and
remain standalone. For `disable`, only `expected_store_version` is required.
Do not add either field to the business Object just to satisfy source inference.
Business state uses its own record CAS input and `conditional_update`; the two
version tokens are distinct and both mutations remain in one Runtime Action
transaction.

Do not put protocol or infrastructure identifiers in Action input: `id`,
`request_id`, `trace_id`, `correlation_id`, `idempotency_key`, `workspace_id`,
`principal_id`, `record_id`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `session_id`,
`database_id`, `db_id`, and `row_id` are rejected. Record targets come from the
Action route, idempotency from `Idempotency-Key`, request identity from Runtime,
and new technical IDs from backend code. Stable business numbers remain
legitimate business fields.

## Roles, data scope and write ownership

Roles contain exact Permission grants, and every grant carries its own scope:

```json
{"roles": {"reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner", "case_attachment.read;owner"]}}
```

The only scope values are `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, and
`target_org`. The Role's same-key Action Permission is the only authored
allowlist. Plane reverse-derives `authorization.allowed_roles`, registers the
Action Permission definition, and never invents a Role grant or scope. Authoring
`Action.roles` is rejected as a duplicate source.

Object write policy is compiler-owned:

- an Object written by a Handler is `action_only` and has no Runtime CRUD
  behavior;
- every other Object is `direct_crud` and receives a Runtime CRUD behavior;
- a direct create/update/delete/restore Role permission or entrypoint mutation
  on a Handler-written Object is a blocking ownership conflict.

Plane expands Role grants into one scoped data-permission container per declared Role/Object.
That container is compiler-owned: the model declares each exact
Permission and scope once as `roles.<role>[] = "<permission_key>;<data_scope>"` and never repeats the
expanded Object policy.

Never author `config.write_policy`, role-level `data_scope`, `scope_overrides`,
`data_permissions` or `reference_permissions`. Handler roles use their explicit
same-key Action grant without receiving direct CRUD mutation permissions.

## Relation reference input

A `relation->target` field is also the complete model input for a reusable
reference selector. Plane derives an exact reference policy only when the role
can write the source Object and read the target Object; duplicate
source/field/target policies collapse to one stable identity.

The frontend calls
`GET /records/{sourceObjectKey}/fields/{relationFieldKey}/options`
with the raw user `query`. It never supplies a target Object, display field,
permission, SQL wildcard or `LIKE` expression. Runtime resolves the relation,
enforces the reference and target row/field policies, escapes `%`, `_` and the
escape character, then creates a parameterized case-insensitive contains
predicate. The component renders only the returned `{"id":"…","name":"…"}`
items.

## Report SQL

Prefer one source-owned file instead of an escaped SQL string:

```json
{"reports": {
  "part_usage": {
    "audience_roles": ["report_reader"],
    "object_sql_v1": {
      "sql_file": "backend/reports/part_usage.sql",
      "parameters": {"status": "text!"}
    }
  }
}}
```

The path must be exactly `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`, canonical,
project-local and non-symlink. Plane normalizes line endings, hashes the source
and embeds SQL in the full Runtime contract. `sql_file` and `sql` are mutually
exclusive.

Plane derives the result schema and preserves SQL SELECT order. Optional
`result_schema` entries are semantic overrides keyed by SELECT alias and do not
control output ordering.

Quote every model-derived Object and field identifier with MySQL backticks,
including ``FROM `lead` l``, ``JOIN `order` o``, and qualified field references
such as ``l.`status```. This is mandatory even for ordinary stable keys: whether
the current parser treats a key as a keyword is not part of the authoring
contract. Keep aliases, parameter names, and result aliases as unquoted stable
keys.

Object SQL may reference only business fields explicitly declared under the
source Object's `fields`. Runtime-owned storage/scope columns
`owner_user_id`/`owner_org_id` are not project-declarable or Report-projectable
columns. Record-envelope `id` is available only as an internal JOIN, filter,
ordering, or COUNT operand and cannot be returned raw. Runtime applies owner/
organization permission scope before executing the Report. Every optional
`result_schema` entry overrides semantics for an existing SQL output alias.

Each `audience_roles` Role must grant `report.query.execute;all` as the exact
executable entry Permission, in addition to every source Object
`*.read;<requirement-selected-scope>` and required field-read policy. Audience
membership and source data access never authorize the Report query route by
themselves.

## Empty values and commands

Omit empty strings, arrays and objects. Omit absent `input`, `output`,
`permissions`, `config`, `preconditions` and optional collections; Plane
creates required empty internal structures. `false` and `0` remain legal only
when they are deliberate business values.

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <module> [--allow-destructive]
```

`model plan` is the no-HTTP repair loop. It runs the same loader, Ledger graph,
authoring checks, Project Contract projection, Runtime Manifest compiler and
source-owner validators used by apply. Its stdout `artifact` is a path relative
to the supplied `--project` root (also declared by
`artifact_relative_to: "--project"`), including on a non-zero repair result.
`apply model` atomically converges the
generated Ledger; an item absent from the model is a destructive deletion and
requires `--allow-destructive`.

Capability assembly remains progressive: choose from bounded summaries, load
only selected focused definitions, and let Plane compile ownership, module
closure and digests. Never author or cache a capability assembly in the model.

`templates/backend-model-handler-minimal/model.json.tmpl` is the directly
loadable two-Object Handler starter.
# Authorization and behavior ownership

Keep Action invocation, exact Permission grants, field policy, frontend
navigation, assurance and execution ownership separate.

In backend-model V3:

- the Role's exact `<action_key>;<data_scope>` array entry is the single
  authored Handler allowlist. Never write `Action.roles` or
  `authorization.allowed_roles`; Plane reverse-derives both the allowlist and
  the complete internal authorization contract from Role grants.
- `handler.access` is the minimum Object/operation EffectAuthority. Do not also
  write `handler.data_access`.
- an ordinary Role is an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` strings;
  each Action or CRUD Permission has its own `data_scope`.
- Plane derives the Action Permission definition, reference policies, Handler
  EffectAuthority, behavior tuple and Object write policy. It never invents a
  Role grant or scope value.

Module HTTP entrypoints obey the same exact-grant rule. Before assigning a
verification step to an actor, look up the exact route in the implementation
packet's `verification.routes`; when `authorization.permission` is non-empty,
that actor's Role must carry `required_role_grant.compact`. An Object read/export
grant, Report `audience_roles` membership, Workflow assignment, or successful
login does not authorize a different executable entrypoint. In particular,
`GET /notification/inbox` requires `notification.inbox.list;all`, and
`POST /report/{reportKey}/query` requires `report.query.execute;all` in addition
to each source Object's requirement-selected `*.read;<scope>` grant. The Inbox
`all` grant selects the executable policy; Notification still binds durable
mailbox reads to the authenticated user and workspace.

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "case_reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner"]
  },
  "actions": {
    "case.approve": {
      "kind": "record_operation",
      "handler": {
        "reason": "Approval verifies eligibility and records a durable decision",
        "access": {
          "case": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
          "case_decision": ["create"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Read operations are `get`, `get_for_update`, `optional`, `list`, `exists`, and
`count`. Write operations are `create`, `update`, `conditional_update`,
`delete`, and `restore`. Locking is not mutation authority. Existing-record
update/delete/restore requires `get_for_update` or `conditional_update`.

Use `object_operation` when no existing record target is supplied and
`record_operation` for a routed record target. Route record ID, workspace,
principal, request, trace and idempotency identities are Runtime/protocol
context and are rejected as Action business input.

A Handler-written Object is `action_only`; its allowed role must explicitly
hold the Handler Action's same-key scoped grant but no direct CRUD permission.
Every other Object is `direct_crud`. Never widen a role or add direct CRUD
merely to satisfy a Handler.

## Scope is an SQL mutation boundary

Treat data-scope enforcement as part of the repository operation, not as
response filtering. `all` means no additional data-scope `WHERE`; workspace,
caller filters and target IDs remain mandatory. Generated reads for `owner`,
`org`, `org_child` and `target_org` must combine the compiled predicate with
those conditions. Existing-record update, delete and restore capabilities must
first select the requested single ID or bounded ID batch with the same scope,
then execute the mutation with that predicate still present in its `UPDATE` or
`DELETE`. Batch target counts must match the authorized selection; any missing
or out-of-scope target fails the whole transaction without partial writes.

Never satisfy scope acceptance by loading unscoped rows and filtering them in
project code. Tests must prove an allowed ID succeeds, an out-of-scope ID is
unchanged, mixed allowed/denied batches roll back atomically, and the repository
query/mutation carries the compiled non-`all` predicate or proves that `all`
contains only workspace, caller-filter and target-ID conditions.

Organization claims are trusted Runtime facts,
not request fields or guessed headers. Sensitive fields remain fail-closed and
their explicit policy comes from the active Authoring Definition.

After implementation, map confirmed PRD authorization boundaries to focused
business-flow tests: actor, target, expected grant/scope, result or denial, and
unchanged durable state after rejection. Use real Identity-backed principals;
Blueprint declarations are not assignment evidence.
# Verification evidence levels

Read this contract during model/apply and before authoring `backend/tests/businessflow`; do not defer it until verify after project-owned source is frozen. The implementation packet's `evidence_contract` is the machine-readable marker grammar and flow-specific required-operation projection of these semantics.

Use this ladder for every verification check and final claim. Each level includes the lower levels, but an artifact reaches a level only when its current proof exists and is bound to the current source/model/Runtime identity.

## Ladder

- `L0_declared`: the capability exists in requirements, model metadata, or source. This proves intent only.
- `L1_delivery_verified`: source finalization is current; format, lint, vet, tests, and packaging pass through `verify`. This proves structural/release closure, not behavior.
- `L2_api_verified`: the operation executes through the real managed Runtime with a real session and its durable result is read back through the typed API or database. A denied/error/conflict case proves unchanged durable state; an idempotency case proves one effect after replay.
- `L3_scenario_verified`: every in-scope business-flow case executes end to end on real Runtime data. Each case starts from explicit preconditions, performs the ordered business actions, and observes its terminal durable result; requirement-defined denial, scope and failure branches are included.
- `L4_browser_verified`: reserved for the authorized offline export center when the project already provides a supported local browser verification path. Other browser-layer UI verification remains outside this Skill.
- `L5_restart_verified`: the critical L3 journey subset and sessions remain correct after a managed Runtime restart, with durable state read back and the critical cases rerun.

## Claim rules

- Never call L0/L1 output `verified`, `accepted`, `working`, `scenario_verified`, or `done`; say `declared` or `delivery_verified`.
- Never infer L2/L3 from a test name, source inspection, metadata checklist, `verify`, package receipt, Runtime health, HTTP 2xx alone, TODO prose, or TODO checker success.
- Never count a click, toast, queued job, emitted event, waiting Workflow, metadata-only import/export record, or local state change as the terminal business effect.
- Report skipped checks as skipped. Do not fold them into a higher level.
- Report coverage only with its exact include scope. A subset percentage is not whole-project coverage.
- Treat missing, empty, partial, stale, unbound, contradictory, or hand-written summary evidence as non-passing.

## L3 evidence requirements

For every business-flow case, bind project-local evidence to the current source digest and Runtime delivery identity. Record its requirement/flow ID, test name/path, actor/role, ordered actions, permission and data scope, persistence probe, terminal result, and audit/receipt identity when applicable.

For non-`none` data scope, provide at least two distinguishable owners and two scope groups when the rule separates them, plus records inside and outside the actor's allowed scope. A single actor, team, owner, or record cannot prove a scope boundary.

For mutations:

- success requires different before/after state and a successful read-back;
- denied, validation, and conflict cases require identical before/after state;
- idempotent replay requires the replay state to equal the first successful after-state;
- restart persistence requires the post-restart state to equal the accepted pre-restart state.

## Minimum terminal level

A Delivery Batch requires current L3 for every in-scope business flow and L5 for every changed or affected critical flow marked restart-sensitive. Unchanged flows may reference prior evidence only when it is still bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity; every changed flow and affected regression boundary must reach the same level in the current batch. Whole-product completion may be claimed only when no Requirement ID remains deferred. When the authorized offline export center changes frontend source, its focused tests and smallest relevant build/typecheck are mandatory; reach L4 only when the project already provides a supported local browser path. Other frontend-owned defects remain findings for the frontend owner.
# Business-flow verification and terminal policy

Read this file completely during `apply` before authoring `backend/tests/businessflow`, and again on entry to `verify`, `done`, or terminal review after a repair. Every required business-flow source file must exist and pass the implementation packet's `business_flow_compile` command before `apply finalize`. After finalization, `verify` is read-and-run only; any project-owned source change makes the receipt stale and starts a new repair iteration that must repeat focused tests, business-flow compile, and finalization.

The implementation packet's compact verification core owns public URL composition, Action-only setup reachability, the project-focused route index, and the BF01-BF08 evidence contract. During apply and before authoring business-flow source, consume `evidence_contract`: `row_required`, `allowed_phases`, `flow_id_pattern`, `required_flows`, `step.allowed_sources`, `step.requirement_id_pattern`, and `flow_contracts.*` are the complete machine-readable marker grammar enforced by verify. Each flow contract gives its minimum step count; BF08 additionally publishes all seven exact `required_operations`, each required `source` and observation schema, shared job-ID equality, and its forbidden shortcut. Read each `minimum_read_plan` shard exactly once after checking its published bytes and SHA-256; each contains only its listed `route_keys`. Do not enumerate or read unlisted route artifacts or the full source route catalog: `route_catalog` binds that complete catalog by contract version, count, and SHA-256 while the focused index is derived from the current compiled manifest. Copy `harness_template.path` verbatim to `backend/tests/businessflow/harness_test.go`; it supplies transport, initial Workspace administrator login/password rotation, record/workflow decoders, Action calls, governed-operation headers, and evidence emission. `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_URL` is the managed listener base URL, `url_composition.base_path` is the release-bound managed entrypoint prefix (currently the explicit empty string), and every `routes.*.path` is an absolute unprefixed mux path. Build a request URL only as `strings.TrimRight(baseURL, "/") + base_path + route.path`; never inject `/api`, `/api/v1`, or another frontend alias.

The same guide owns response and actor-grant contracts. Decode record lists from
top-level `items`; `items[].data` contains business fields, while `id`,
`created_at`, `updated_at`, `owner_user_id`, and `owner_org_id` remain top-level
record metadata. Never read legacy `fields` or merge all top-level keys into
business data. For every module HTTP step, select the guide route by exact
method/path and require the chosen actor Role to contain
`routes.<route>.required_role_grant.compact`. Report audience/data/field
permissions are additional constraints, not replacements for the route entry
Permission. Thus Inbox list uses `notification.inbox.list;all` for every
materialized managed verification actor—including acceptance/admin Roles used
only for setup or identity delivery—and Object SQL
query uses `report.query.execute;all` plus source read/field grants.

Runtime collection shapes are route-specific. `GET /workflow/tasks` and
`GET /workflow/team-tasks` return a top-level JSON array; decode directly into
`[]workflowTask` with the harness `decodeWorkflowTasks` helper—there is no
`items` or `tasks` envelope. Records lists remain top-level objects with
`items`. Records pagination normalizes `page<=0` to `1`, non-positive or
non-integer `page_size` to `25`, and values above `200` to `200`; oversize is a
successful clamped request, not a `400`. Assert the returned `page_size` and
item bound.

Every route index entry lists its exact `required_headers`. In particular,
governed Report export prepare requires `Idempotency-Key`, a non-empty
`X-Operation-Reason`, and `X-Operation-Confirmation: confirmed`. Pass these
through `runtimeRequestOptions`; never add confirmation to a route whose
machine contract does not require it.

For an `action_only` Object, Workspace administrator authority does not unlock direct
`POST/PATCH/DELETE /records`; Runtime returns
`backend.mutation.action_required`. Build ordinary business-flow setup through
the published Object/Record Action catalog and the implementation core's
`setup_contract.available_actions`. Create required business identities and
organizations only through authored Identity HandlerDelivery and
OrganizationDelivery Actions. If those exact Action inputs cannot establish a
required precondition, repair the Blueprint and Handler surface before
finalization, rerun `model plan`, and follow
`setup_contract.post_apply_repair`: exit-0 `evolution_review_required` means
inspect its immutable audit and reapply with the exact SHA plus a non-empty
reason; only `implementation_ready` or `applied` resumes source work. Its
machine contract names `materialization_state:not_materialized` and
`deferred_finalization_state:deferred_unfinalized_source`. The latter is valid
only when the audit proves that the old delivery had no finalization receipt;
it preserves in-progress source without trusting it, and `apply finalize`
remains mandatory. Deleting an audit-bound prior receipt to force deferral is
forbidden. For an
elapsed-time/“N days later” flow that cannot wait in an isolated Runtime, use
`setup_contract.elapsed_time_verification`: the narrowly scoped internal
service Action may accept optional `evaluation_time`, the ordinary Scheduler
path omits it, and production defaults to real current time. Never use a global
clock override or grant this seam to a human. Never inject records, roles,
users, organizations, or historical timestamps through Runtime bootstrap or a
startup fixture.

## One verification model

Verification uses project-owned business-flow test cases and one CLI-owned,
temporary evidence protocol. There is no acceptance denominator, generic case runner,
carry-forward/stale-report workflow, or project-owned second evidence ledger.

Each current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary has one stable flow ID and one or more ordinary project-owned test cases under `backend/**`. Group cross-module cases under `backend/tests/businessflow/` when that makes ownership clearer; keep focused unit cases beside their source. A flow case starts from explicit preconditions, uses the requirement's real actor and scope, performs the ordered business actions, and asserts the terminal business result through durable read-back. It is not a list of disconnected endpoint checks. An unchanged flow may reuse prior evidence only when the TODO identifies that evidence and proves it remains bound to the current baseline delivery/model identity.

The current-batch business-flow inventory and affected regression closure must cover:

- every current-batch happy path from initial state through all required transitions to its terminal observable result;
- every requirement-defined alternate or rejection branch, including authorization, data-scope, validation and conflict behavior;
- unchanged durable state after a denied, invalid or failed action;
- idempotent replay, transaction rollback, concurrency, restart/resume, notification, schedule, file, integration, Object SQL Report, offline export submission, actor-owned job-list visibility or completed download only when the accepted flow actually depends on it;
- current-batch Requirement ID → Feature key → flow ID → test name/path traceability, plus baseline references for unchanged affected flows.

Do not multiply cases for platform internals that no business requirement observes. One flow case may prove several operations when they are steps of the same business journey. Conversely, do not call a set of isolated unit tests complete when no case executes the required journey end to end.

## Direct commands

Finalize source after focused implementation tests, then run:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

`verify` runs the complete backend Go test tree with the delivery's Domain SDK build constraint, packages the verified source, proves an initial healthy start, stops it, proves a healthy restart of the same package/database cohort, and finally stops it. When `backend/tests/businessflow/*_test.go` exists, the CLI compiles that package once from the verified source and runs the same test binary against both healthy Runtime processes before stopping them. Those tests may skip only when `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_URL` is absent during the ordinary pre-package test pass; when present, require `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_PHASE` to be `initial` or `restart` and use the supplied URL. This package is a black-box Runtime boundary: direct imports of project `actions`, generated capability/data fakes, `database/sql`, or database drivers fail verification. Keep those imports in focused unit/integration tests outside `backend/tests/businessflow`.

On each managed run every BF01-BF08 test emits exactly one line containing
`DOMAINRY_BF_EVIDENCE=` followed by its JSON row (use `t.Log`, never credentials):
The combined public contract is
[business-flow-evidence-v1.schema.json](contracts/business-flow-evidence-v1.schema.json).

```json
{
  "phase": "initial",
  "flow_id": "BF01",
  "status": "passed",
  "steps": [{
    "id": "<stable-step-id>",
    "operation": "<semantic-operation>",
    "source": "runtime.action",
    "status": "passed",
    "requirements": ["1"],
    "observations": {"durable_result_read_back": true}
  }]
}
```

Allowed sources are `runtime.records`, `runtime.action`, `runtime.workflow`,
`runtime.scheduler`, `runtime.report`, `runtime.data_exchange`,
`runtime.identity`, `runtime.navigation`, and `project_handler`. Every flow and
step must pass; step IDs are unique inside a flow, requirements are positive
numeric public requirement IDs, and observations are business oracles rather
than request/status trivia. The CLI rejects missing, duplicate, malformed,
wrong-phase, unknown-source, failed, or incomplete BF01-BF08 evidence and
combines both accepted phases as `domainry-business-flow-evidence-v1`.

A governed export flow uses all seven exact operations:
`report.prepare`, `report.prepare.unauthorized_denied`,
`data_exchange.job.owner_bound`, `data_exchange.job.completed`,
`data_exchange.job.download`, `data_exchange.job.foreign_download_denied`, and
`artifact.csv.content_validated`. Preserve one `job_id` across prepare, owner,
completed and download; prove prepare `accepted`, requester ownership,
`job_status:"completed"`, a non-empty actual job download with `text/csv`
content type, and both denial observations with `access_denied:true` and
`different_actor:true`. Content proves `csv_parsed`,
`row_count_matches_report`, and `content_hash_verified`. Do not satisfy this
with a hand-built CSV or forbidden `records.csv_export`.

The verify result includes `domainry-verify-telemetry-v1` elapsed stages,
cache decisions, and first-failure owner. Current verification/package receipts
are reused only after complete delivery, model/source tree, Runtime manifest,
dependency/build-lock, signature, and bundle artifact validation. Runtime start,
both business-flow phases, same-cohort restart, and final stop are never cached.

The CLI supplies immutable delivery, package-receipt, verification-receipt, project-source and database-identity values under the `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_*` prefix. It also supplies the child-only authentication contract `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_WORKSPACE_ID`, `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_WORKSPACE_CODE`, `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_APPLICATION_KEY`, `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_WORKSPACE_ADMIN_LOGIN_ID`, `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_INITIAL_WORKSPACE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`, and `DOMAINRY_MANAGED_RUNTIME_CHANGED_WORKSPACE_ADMIN_PASSWORD`.
