# Identity user and reporting line

> **TL;DR** — Identity User itself owns the person's primary organization placement, personnel facts, direct manager, and reporting path. There is no separate Workforce profile or assignment model.

## Ownership

`domainry-identity` owns `identity_user`. Besides login identity and account status, the same User record owns:

- `org_id` — the user's one primary organization unit;
- `manager_user_id` — the user's direct manager, referencing another User;
- `reporting_path` — Identity-derived, persisted reporting-tree path;
- `worker_no`, `worker_type`, `work_status`, `start_date`, and `end_date` — personnel facts when required.

The organization tree and reporting tree are independent. Moving an organization node changes organization paths. Changing `manager_user_id` changes the user's reporting path and atomically rewrites descendant reporting paths. An organization unit does not carry a leader user ID, and no organization node is created for an individual person.

## Blueprint boundary

Runtime exposes `identity_user` as an external relation target. A project may reference a User where a business record needs an owner, applicant, operator, or approver. It must not declare a second employee/personnel table merely to duplicate Identity-owned fields.

The Blueprint never authors Identity operational state: no `identity_bootstrap`, users, personnel rows, organization units, managers, credentials, or live role assignments. Provision those through Identity module/SaaS APIs and fixtures.

Business-specific facts still belong to business objects. For example, commission grade, training certification, shift preference, and domain-specific qualifications may live in a one-to-one business Profile related to `identity_user`; the Profile must not copy the User fields listed above.

## Workflow manager resolution

`manager_of` reads a user-valued record field and resolves that User's `manager_user_id`. `initiator_manager` resolves the actual process initiator's `manager_user_id`. Runtime ignores missing or inactive manager accounts and applies the node's `empty_assignee_policy`. Neither resolver infers a manager from organization membership, role name, job title, or an organization-unit leader.

## Data authorization

Roles grant exact Permissions, each with its own `data_scope`. Users are not separately granted organizations through role-to-organization or user-to-organization assignment tables. Runtime stores stable `owner_user_id` and `owner_org_id` system columns on each business record. Identity supplies the current organization tree for `org_child` and the trusted support-organization tree for `target_org`; neither policy reads a path copied into the business record. Reporting-line membership is not a separate authoring scope.

## Authority and limits

`domainry-identity` owns User persistence, reporting-tree validation, and personnel lifecycle facts. `domainry-identity-sdk` owns identity projection and authorization contracts. Runtime consumes User facts for workflow resolution and policy enforcement; Plane only publishes business metadata and project-role policy.
# Scheduler

Scheduler owns recurring calendar/interval planning and durable run/retry
lifecycle. Runtime Record Timer separately owns waits tied to one record or
Workflow node. Never build a project cron daemon.

```json
{
  "scheduled_jobs": {
    "expire_cards": {
      "status": "enabled",
      "target_type": "workflow",
      "target_key": "membership_expiry",
      "schedule": {
        "expression": "0 1 * * *",
        "timezone": "Asia/Shanghai"
      },
      "missed_window_policy": "catch_up_one",
      "max_attempts": 3,
      "timeout_seconds": 300
    }
  }
}
```

Job identity and name are compiler-expanded. Target type is `workflow` or
`report_snapshot_refresh`; direct Actions, CRUD and report export are not
Scheduler targets. A scheduled Workflow declares a scheduled trigger and owns
the business Action it invokes. When that Workflow uses an internal execution
Role, bind it with Workflow `run_as`; declare the Role with
`audience: "service"` and `assignment_mode: "system_managed"`, and omit
`provision_to_workspaces` (preferred) or set it to `false`. Scheduler does not
turn that Role into a tenant-login actor.

The schedule shape selects its kind: `expression` means cron,
`interval_seconds` means interval, `time_of_day` alone means daily, and adding
`day_of_week` or `day_of_month` means weekly or monthly. Plane derives the
single fixed `type` discriminator; do not author it. Prefer the calendar shapes
with an IANA timezone when they express the business clock; use interval for
elapsed cadence and cron only for other supported calendar expressions.
Missing timezone defaults to UTC.

The inlined machine contracts expose these layers separately:
`plane.blueprint_collection/scheduled_jobs` is the compact map value authored
in `backend/model/*.json`; `scheduler.blueprint_source_capability/

after Plane expands identity/defaults. Both use the same nested schedule
shapes. Neither exposes Runtime's flattened `schedule_type`, and both preserve
shape-derived `schedule.type` as compiler-owned. You must never author `trigger_type`;
the Runtime compiler adds the fixed `scheduled` value only to the emitted
Scheduler definition.

`skip`, `catch_up_one`, and `catch_up_bounded` describe windows missed while
Scheduler was unavailable. `max_attempts` describes retries of one claimed
window. They are independent, and downstream behavior remains idempotent by
the scheduled window identity.

Acceptance correlates a terminal Scheduler run to durable Workflow/Report
evidence and, when applicable, an independently read committed business effect.
A cursor advance, retrying run or zero required effect is not success.

When acceptance depends on an elapsed-time rule such as “N days later”, design
the first Blueprint so a short-lived isolated Runtime can prove that business

This is not a generic test clock. Do not add a global clock override, allow a
human caller to choose business time, make Scheduler pass `evaluation_time`,
inject historical timestamps through bootstrap, or create a startup historical
fixture. The `scheduler.authoring` machine contract

Elapsed-time verification may declare an optional `evaluation_time` datetime on

that input, so production uses the host-provided current
time. Only a bounded black-box verification may supply it; a global clock

# Workflow

Workflow owns durable multi-step processes, approval, waiting, retry and resume.
Use one transactional Handler for atomic work that does not wait.

## Compact V3 graph

```json
{
  "workflows": {
    "refund_approval": {
      "enabled": true,
      "run_as": "refund_manager",
      "trigger": {"type": "manual"},
      "action": {"type": "workflow_graph"},
      "trigger_contract": {"type": "manual", "object_key": "refund"},
      "graph": {
        "nodes": {
          "submitted": {"type": "trigger"},
          "manager_approval": {
            "type": "approval",
            "contract": {
              "approval": {
                "mode": "any",
                "empty_assignee_policy": "fail",
                "resolvers": [{"type": "role", "role_key": "refund_manager"}]
              }
            }
          },
          "settle": {
            "type": "action",
            "contract": {
              "action": {
                "action_key": "refund.settle",
                "input": {"decision": "approved"},
                "on_error": "fail"
              }
            }
          },
          "reject": {
            "type": "action",
            "contract": {
              "action": {
                "action_key": "refund.reject",
                "input": {
                  "decision": "$workflow.approval_decision",
                  "comment": "$workflow.approval_comment"
                },
                "on_error": "fail"
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "edges": {
          "submitted_approval": {"source": "submitted", "target": "manager_approval"},
          "approval_settle": {"source": "manager_approval", "target": "settle", "branch": "approved"},
          "approval_reject": {"source": "manager_approval", "target": "reject", "branch": "rejected"}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Workflow, node and edge identities are map keys. Plane injects their internal
identity fields. For an Action node it derives `object_key` from the declared
Action and derives the routed `$record.id` target for record Actions; do not
author either technical field. Node input contains only business parameters.

`run_as` is a Role key, not a tenant-login provisioning request. For an
internal execution identity, declare that Role with `audience: "service"` and
`assignment_mode: "system_managed"`, and omit `provision_to_workspaces`
(preferred) or set it to `false`. Runtime resolves the internal
`workflow:<workflow_key>` subject through Identity under that Role and fails
closed when it cannot resolve it. Preserve these internal semantics; never
change the Role to a human audience or manual assignment to make validation
pass.

Approval resolvers are chosen from the business subject: explicit users,
declared role membership, a user-valued record field, `manager_of`, or
`initiator_manager`. `first_match` is ordered fallback; `union` combines all
candidates. Use `empty_assignee_policy: fail` unless bypass/admin fallback is an
accepted business rule.

Graph binding is fail-closed. Every required Action input must come from the
trigger context or a prior node available on every incoming path. Approval wire
decisions are `approved`, `rejected`, and `returned`. A waiting process or open
task is intermediate evidence, not completion.

Approval outputs are process-wide bindings: use
`$workflow.approval_decision` and `$workflow.approval_comment` on terminal
branches. A node-local guess such as `$manager_approval.comment` or
`$director_approval.comment` is not a published binding and fails validation.

When a requirement says a person approves or rejects after waiting, the approval
node and its durable Runtime task are mandatory. Separate synchronous approve/reject Handlers,
a pending Object, or `approval_required` metadata alone cannot
replace the Workflow; terminal branch nodes may invoke the existing atomic
Handlers for their business effects.

Acceptance proves resolved assignees, unauthorized decision denial, each
terminal branch, durable process/task state, Handler business effects, retry and
restart resume. Do not replace an expressible graph with one giant Handler or
invent approval tokens and private workflow endpoints.

# Guarded workspace provisioning

Runtime and embedded Identity create the installation Workspace, the
Blueprint's eligible human Workspace Role directory, initial company/store,
one explicit administrator assignment, commercial configuration, and
idempotency receipt in one host database transaction. The
administrator credential is generated by Identity and claimed once only after
the host reports commit. That Workspace is the tenant boundary;
tenant and workspace are not separate domain concepts. Projects never reproduce
that flow with record Actions or direct Identity writes.

Never author a `tenant` or `workspace` Object/table, a project-owned
`tenant_id`/`workspace_id`, a relation to such an Object, or a baseline
projection whose only purpose is to copy workspace identity. Requirements that
say tenant map to the Runtime-owned workspace context. An independently
required company, customer, merchant, store, or other business aggregate uses
its real domain name and must have facts or a lifecycle beyond workspace
identity.

Only human-login roles may be materialized into new workspaces:

```json
{
  "roles": {
    "store_admin": {
      "grants": ["order.read;all", "order.update;all"],
      "audience": "user",
      "assignment_mode": "manual",
      "provision_to_workspaces": true
    }
  }
}
```

Every new model also selects the initial administrator Role explicitly in its
project fragment:

```json
{
  "project": {
    "id": "orders",
    "initial_workspace_administrator_role": "store_admin"
  }
}
```

The selected Role must exist, set `provision_to_workspaces: true`, use
`audience: "any"` or `"user"`, use `assignment_mode: "manual"`, and have no
`required_binding_key`. A `business_profile` Role may be an ordinary Workspace
login Role, but cannot be the initial administrator because its active profile
binding does not exist yet. Likewise, `request_only` and `system_managed` Roles
cannot be assigned during bootstrap. Never infer or select it by `_admin`
suffix, risk level, Permission shape, declaration order, or “first Role”.

In backend model v3, the compact Role grant array is shorthand for
`audience:"any"`, `assignment_mode:"manual"`, and
`provision_to_workspaces:true`. Use the extended form above when the role must
be explicitly user-only.
Non-human/system roles must use the extended object with their explicit
audience and `assignment_mode: "system_managed"`; omit
`provision_to_workspaces` (preferred) or set it to `false`. A Workflow binds the
role by key through `run_as`, including when Scheduler targets that Workflow.
Do not repair an internal role by changing it to a human audience or manual
assignment. Internal Roles remain in the complete post-bootstrap directory but
are excluded from the initial Workspace login-role subset.

Initial first-store business records are optional and keyed once. They are
inserted in the same transaction as Identity's company, first store, eligible
human Role directory, explicit administrator assignment, and Runtime commercial
configuration:

```json
{
  "workspace_provisioning": {
    "first_store_operating_configuration": {
      "object_key": "operating_config",
      "input_bindings": {
        "currency": "currency",
        "timezone": "timezone"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Every binding key must be a declared non-relation/non-user business field and
every binding value is a stable application-bootstrap input key. A required
bound field declares a valid default so managed verification can initialize an
isolated Workspace with `{}` while Runtime applies the descriptor defaults.
The compiler derives the exact input type, enum, numeric range, string length,
pattern, format, required/default contract and input hash from those Object
fields. It then generates one fixed `WorkspaceBootstrapParticipant`; Runtime
projects the same descriptor to `POST /workspaces` and validates
`INITIAL_WORKSPACE_APPLICATION_BOOTSTRAP_JSON` against it.

There is no authored scope, object selector, Organization ID, owner field,
Workspace database ID, expression language, or arbitrary JSON Schema map.
Runtime always injects the new Workspace and first-store owner, and requires
the generated participant to return exactly one record for every declared
capability.

Passwords and credentials are never Blueprint/model or initialization-input
values. Runtime/protocol code owns provisioning request identity and
idempotency. Identity generates the one-time initial password, Runtime reports
the real transaction outcome, and only a verified commit permits one claim and
delivery through the host credential seam. Rollback and expiry destroy the
volatile credential; replay requires a reset instead of redisclosing it.

The path must be exactly `backend/reports/<report-key>.sql`, canonical,
project-local and non-symlink. Plane normalizes line endings, hashes the source
and embeds SQL in the full Runtime contract. `sql_file` and `sql` are mutually
exclusive.

Plane derives the result schema and preserves SQL SELECT order. Optional
`result_schema` entries are semantic overrides keyed by SELECT alias and do not
control output ordering.

Quote every model-derived Object and field identifier with MySQL backticks,
including ``FROM `lead` l``, ``JOIN `order` o``, and qualified field references
such as ``l.`status```. This is mandatory even for ordinary stable keys: whether
the current parser treats a key as a keyword is not part of the authoring
contract. Keep aliases, parameter names, and result aliases as unquoted stable
keys.

Object SQL may reference only business fields explicitly declared under the
source Object's `fields`. Runtime-owned storage/scope columns
`owner_user_id`/`owner_org_id` are not project-declarable or Report-projectable
columns. Record-envelope `id` is available only as an internal JOIN, filter,
ordering, or COUNT operand and cannot be returned raw. Runtime applies owner/
organization permission scope before executing the Report. Every optional
`result_schema` entry overrides semantics for an existing SQL output alias.

Each `audience_roles` Role must grant `report.query.execute;all` as the exact
executable entry Permission, in addition to every source Object
`*.read;<requirement-selected-scope>` and required field-read policy. Audience
membership and source data access never authorize the Report query route by
themselves.

## Empty values and commands

Omit empty strings, arrays and objects. Omit absent `input`, `output`,
`permissions`, `config`, `preconditions` and optional collections; Plane
creates required empty internal structures. `false` and `0` remain legal only
when they are deliberate business values.

```text
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --go-module-path <module> [--allow-destructive]
```

`model plan` is the no-HTTP repair loop. It runs the same loader, Ledger graph,
authoring checks, Project Contract projection, Runtime Manifest compiler and
source-owner validators used by apply. Its stdout `artifact` is a path relative
to the supplied `--project` root (also declared by
`artifact_relative_to: "--project"`), including on a non-zero repair result.
`apply model` atomically converges the
generated Ledger; an item absent from the model is a destructive deletion and
requires `--allow-destructive`.

Capability assembly remains progressive: choose from bounded summaries, load
only selected focused definitions, and let Plane compile ownership, module
closure and digests. Never author or cache a capability assembly in the model.

`templates/backend-model-handler-minimal/model.json.tmpl` is the directly
loadable two-Object Handler starter.
